messages:
Priya: quick question — before i flip the new routing fallback i want to validate precedence assumptions. trying to reason through: org-level default=false, project 'payments'=true, route '/pay/express'=unspecified, model override for 'tiny-quant' = false. which value wins for an incoming /pay/express request that selects tiny-quant via routing?
Sam: short answer in our current design: most-specific scope wins. so route > model > project > org.
Mika: wait does model count as more specific than route? previously we discussed route-specific model pins which made route take precedence over model setting.
Alex: tagging the config we use:```json
{
  "org_default": false,
  "projects": { "payments": { "default": true } },
  "routes": { "/pay/express": { /* no explicit flag */ } },
  "models": { "tiny-quant": { "force_off": true } }
}```
Priya: yep that matches. my worry: routing can pick tiny-quant after audience selection, but if model-level `force_off` exists should that override a project opt-in?
Sam: in todays runtime the model-level `force_off` is absolute — it prevents loading the model regardless of route/project. so model.force_off > project.
Mika: so the final order is route setting (if explicit enable/disable), then model.force flags, then project, then org? that's inconsistent with "most specific wins" phrasing.
Alex: i agree wording was sloppy. better rule: explicit route-level flag wins if present. Otherwise if the selected model has an explicit `force_off/force_on` that wins. Then fallback to project, then org.
Priya: ok that helps. follow-up: canary audiences — if a route has a canary audience that sends 10% to model B, and model B is force_off at model-level, will the canary be skipped or will the 10% fall back to project/model A?
Sam: implementation note: we evaluate audience membership first, then try to instantiate the chosen variant. if chosen variant is unavailable due to force_off we fall back to the next compatible variant per routing policy. if none, then use project/org defaults.
Mika: example scenario please (for docs).
Alex: example snippet we can add to docs:```text
1) Request hits /pay/express in project payments
2) Route has canary: 10% -> tiny-quant (model B), 90% -> standard (model A)
3) User assigned to tiny-quant bucket -> runtime attempts tiny-quant; model-level force_off=true -> runtime skips tiny-quant
4) Fallback policy: try route's alternate (standard). route-level explicit disable would block fallback and instead use project default.```
Priya: perfect. last bits — should we add a lint rule to reject contradictory flags (e.g., route.enable=true + model.force_off=true) or just emit warnings?
Sam: i'd push for warnings for now, because there are valid transient cases during rollouts. but telemetry + lint that surfaces these combinations would be great.
Mika: can ops-bot add an automatic note when someone flips a route-level flag that touches a model with force_off? ops-bot: :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: I can add a webhook to post a warning when a flag flip matches a known model.force_off pattern. want it turned on for payments-only to start?
Priya: yes start payments-only. i'll draft the small docs blurb and add the example. thanks all :raised_hands:
